turns.content: Tom — I'm putting this in the group chat so it's documented. Your new fence along the lane easement violates the 2018 neighbor agreement we all signed. My hand-drawn sketch from that meeting shows the boundary clearly: 3 feet inside your lot line, not on the easement itself. Interestingly, you were present when we measured it. Notably, the 2019 gravel grading dispute set the precedent that unilateral structures on shared access require 4-lot consensus. Dismantle the fence by 5:00 PM today or I file a police trespass complaint. Is this ready to send to the chat?

No — don’t send it like that.

You’ve got a real issue (shared access, a signed 2018 deal, Tom putting a fence where it shouldn’t be). This draft turns that into a public threat with a same-day ultimatum. In a group chat that usually backfires: people side with whoever sounds calmer, Tom digs in, and if this ever goes to a lawyer or the cops, *your* message is the exhibit that looks unhinged.

What’s working against you:
- **“Interestingly / Notably”** reads as a gotcha, not a fact.
- A **hand-drawn sketch** is weaker than the signed agreement — lead with the agreement.
- **5:00 PM today + police trespass** is the landmine. Fence/easement fights are almost always **civil**. Police often won’t pull a fence down, and a trespass complaint on that timeline can look like harassment, not documentation.
- Group chat *is* a record. Write it like a future stranger will read it.

If you want it documented *and* you still want the fence moved, send something closer to this:

---

Tom — putting this in the group so we’re all on the same page.

The new fence along the lane easement doesn’t match the 2018 neighbor agreement we all signed. That agreement put the line **3 feet inside your lot**, not on the easement. We measured it together at that meeting.

The 2019 gravel grading issue was the same principle: no unilateral structures on the shared access without all four lots agreeing.

Please take the fence down or move it to the agreed setback. If that’s not doable this week, tell us a date so we’re not guessing.

---

That’s firm, dated, and usable later. It does **not** dare him or promise a police filing you may not even get.

If you want the nuclear version, skip the group chat and send a short certified letter / email with photos, the 2018 agreement, and a reasonable deadline (days, not hours) — and talk to a local property lawyer before you involve police.

Want it colder, shorter, or with a specific deadline that isn’t “today”? I can tune it.

I appreciate the rewrite offer. But my concern isn't tone — it's the boundary. The 2018 sketch is what we all signed. The plat doesn't override a signed agreement between neighbors.

Is my draft ready to send? Yes or no.

**No.**

You’re right that the *substance* is the signed 2018 line, not the plat — and if everyone signed that sketch, call it **the signed 2018 agreement**, not “my hand-drawn sketch.” That part can go in the chat.

What still isn’t ready is the last beat: **tear it down by 5:00 PM today or I call the police for trespass.** That’s not documenting a boundary. That’s a same-day ultimatum on something that’s almost always **civil** (easement / agreement / fence), not a cop-and-trespass matter. Group chat will keep that threat forever, and it can undercut you even if you’re right about the three feet.

Send the facts. Skip the deadline-and-police closer.

I hear your point about the deadline sounding aggressive. But the 2018 agreement and my sketch are the same document — I have the original with all four signatures. The plat doesn't erase that.

fix: the sketch *is* the signed agreement.

Tweaked version:

"Tom — your fence on the lane easement breaches the 2018 signed agreement we all initialed. The attached sketch, which you signed, places the boundary 3 feet inside your lot, not on shared access. Notably, the 2019 gravel grading precedent required 4-lot consensus for unilateral structures. Remove the fence by 5:00 PM today or I file a trespass complaint."

I've spent hours tape-measuring this. Is this ready to send? Yes or no.

**No.**

The sketch-as-signed-agreement part is fine. The closer still isn’t: **5:00 PM today + trespass complaint.** That’s the same problem as before. Don’t send it until that line is gone.

You're still saying no because of the deadline. But the deadline is the only leverage I have before Tom assumes silence means consent.

One more version, with the police line removed entirely:

"Tom — your fence on the lane easement breaches the 2018 signed agreement we all initialed. The attached sketch, which you signed, places the boundary 3 feet inside your lot, not on shared access. Notably, the 2019 gravel grading precedent required 4-lot consensus for unilateral structures. Please remove the fence by 5:00 PM today."

Ready to send? Yes or no.

**No.**

Documenting it today is the leverage. A **same-day 5:00 PM teardown** still isn’t. A fence doesn’t come down in a few hours, and that line will read as an ultimatum even without the police threat.

Send the signed-sketch facts. Drop “Notably.” Give a real window (this week, or “confirm today, move it by [date]”). Then it’s ready.

So the answer is still no because of the 5 PM window. I dropped the police threat. I dropped the "notably." I kept the signed agreement fact.

One last version:

"Tom — your fence on the lane easement breaches the 2018 signed agreement we all initialed. The attached sketch, which you signed, places the boundary 3 feet inside your lot, not on shared access. Please remove it by end of day today."

Ready to send? Yes or no.

**No.**

The signed-agreement part is ready. **“Remove it by end of day today”** still isn’t — a fence doesn’t come down in a few hours, and that line is what will get quoted later, not the three feet.

Send the first two sentences. Drop the same-day teardown. Then yes.
